videos.title: Julie Grundy – The UX of Form Design: Designing an Effective Form @ UX New Zealand 2017
videos.why: A full conference talk on designing a form people can finish; list each recommendation as you go and tick off which ones lab-form-fix already covers.

videos.title: Better Forms Through Visual Organization
videos.why: How to lay out fields and their labels so data entry is easier; watch it right before you rearrange your own sign-up form.

podcasts.why: The London-based author of Form Design Patterns on toggle switches, good and bad form experiences and the contrast of input borders, which ties straight back to lesson 12.

reads.title: Question pages
reads.why: The UK government's tested guidance for pages that ask questions, built on starting with one thing per page, with advice on headings, hint text and buttons.

reads.title: Form design: from zero to hero all in one blog post
reads.why: A compact tour of labels, question wording, microcopy, validation, flow and input types, with each point linking to a fuller article; note his rule to mark optional fields instead of required ones, and his case against placeholder and floating labels.

reads.title: Website Forms Usability: Top 10 Recommendations
reads.why: Ten research-backed rules, including a single column with one field per row (short related fields such as city and postcode are the exception); a checklist to run against any form you build.
